The two disciplines

Sporting™ Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ imitates hunting. Shooting stands, the marked spots you shoot from, are set out over natural ground: in fields, by woods, on slopes. Targets fly the way a partridge, a duck or a pheasant would, or roll like a hare. Each layout, a group of stands, gives 25 targets: 15 singles and 5 doubles (a double is two targets, so 10 more). The two targets of a double fly together or one after the other.

Compak® Sporting Compak® Sporting is the compact version. Everything happens on one field with 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line. The shooter moves through all five stations and shoots 5 targets at each, 25 per round. A Compak field needs little space, so it is easy for a club to build one.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

You walk a course from stand to stand, and each stand has its own targets. A double can be on report, where your first shot releases the second target, or simultaneous, where both fly at once. A rafale is two targets from the same trap, one right after the other.

Compak® Sporting

You stay on one field and, after each turn, move one station to the right. A double is on report, where your first shot releases the second target, or simultaneous, where both fly at once.

International competitions in both disciplines are usually 200 targets, shot in rounds of 25. In both, you may fire two shots at a single target: if the first shot misses, the second can still break it.

Both disciplines belong to FITASC, the international federation that writes their rules. They share the basics: safety, the gun mount (bringing the gun to cheek and shoulder) and reading the target.

Key points

  • Sporting™: a course over natural ground; each layout gives 25 targets.
  • Compak® Sporting: one field with 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line.
  • An international competition is usually 200 targets, shot in rounds of 25; you may fire twice at a single target.
  • Both disciplines follow the FITASC rules and share the basics: safety, gun mount and reading the target.

Did you know?

Compak® Sporting was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. How many targets does one Sporting™ layout give?

    1. 10
    2. 25
    3. 50
    Answer

    25

    Each layout gives 25 targets: 15 singles and 5 doubles (a double is two targets, so 10 more).

  2. How many traps are there on one Compak field?

    1. Six, lettered A to F
    2. Four, lettered A to D
    3. Ten, two at each station
    Answer

    Six, lettered A to F

    A Compak® Sporting field has 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line.

  3. In which discipline do you walk a course from stand to stand?

    1. Compak® Sporting
    2. Both, in the same way
    3. Sporting™
    Answer

    Sporting™

    In Sporting™ you move from stand to stand over natural ground; in Compak® Sporting you stay on one field and move one station to the right.
